A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we develop a paradigm for MCORAM and other distributed/encrypted protocols, and in particular, establish new connections to FHE and DPF.
MCORAM has been placed on the road to polylogarithmic communication.

MCORAM can be built under the same assumptions as ORAM (i.e., FHE and sub-exponential sized secure two-party computation) and as efficiently as ORAM, while providing an additional layer of flexibility in access control and client-privacy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can enjoy access control and obliviousness simultaneously in the multi-client setting, under the same communication and computation complexities, for the first time.
the virtualization technique proves to be highly versatile: Constructions of MCORAM and DPF have been long sought after, yet we achieve them in one fell swoop.
the virtualization technique enables us to securely outsource large-scale confidential data to a single or multiple untrusted servers while providing controlled access to multiple clients.
